stepsEnglish: For any x, the left side means x is in C, or x is in B but not A.
The right side means x is in B or C, but not in A − C.
When x is in C, both sides contain x.
When x is not in C, both sides contain x precisely when x is in B and not A.
Thus the two sides have the same elements.

items.questionEnglish: 5. Justify the trueness of the statement: “An element of a set can never be a subset of itself.”
stepsEnglish: The empty set ∅ is an element of A.
Every set is a subset of itself, including ∅ ⊆ ∅.
Therefore ∅ is an element of A that is a subset of itself, disproving the claim.

items.questionEnglish: 6. If n(P(A)) = 1024, n(A ∪ B) = 15 and n(P(B)) = 32, then find n(A ∩ B).
stepsEnglish: For a finite set X, n(P(X)) = 2^{n(X)}.
Use n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).

items.questionEnglish: 7. If n(A ∩ B) = 3 and n(A ∪ B) = 10, then find n(P(A∆B)).
stepsEnglish: A∆B consists of elements in exactly one of A and B.
The union contains 10 elements, of which 3 are in both sets.
